title: Safety, Acceptance, Fluency and Efficiency in Human- Robot Interaction
summary: The goal of this study is to evaluate how medical robots can move in ways that people find safe, acceptable, and efficient when interacting with humans. In hospitals and care settings, robots often work close to people, which creates challenges for trust, safety, and smooth cooperation. The study has two parts: an online survey, in which participants watch short videos showing a medical robot interacting either with patients or with healthcare staff, and an in-person study, in which participants evaluate the same types of robot movements on a real robot in a lab.
conditions: Evaluation of safety-, acceptance- and efficiency-oriented movement paradigms for medical robotic systems in the context of human-robot interaction

interventions.name: Online survey for evaluating different robotic movement patterns, separately for the use cases of patient interaction and staff interaction.

Each participant goes through several scenarios with a research-oriented medical robotic system (again separated by use case). criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Medical professionals (e.g., medical students, nursing staff, physicians) employed in a hospital or other medical facility before or during the study (applies only to the “staff interaction” use case); experience with basic procedures in inpatient patient care (applies only to the “staff interaction” use case); Health status: No acute or chronic illnesses that could impair participation (= healthy participants); Vision and hearing: No impairments that would affect the perception of the robot interaction; Language skills: Good German or English skills to understand the study instructions and the questionnaire. Non-German-speaking participants may be included if adequate information is provided in English and written consent is obtained; Consent: Written informed consent to participate in the study after thorough briefing
Exclusion criteria:
Health status: Illnesses that could affect participation or be affected by participation; Visual or hearing impairments: Any limitations that would influence the perception of the interaction; Insufficient language skills: Individuals who do not have adequate German or English language skills to meaningfully evaluate the user interface and the questionnaire; Multiple study load: Participation in other studies with similar demands (to avoid overlap effects)
